```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE, purl = FALSE)
```

shadshiny does not draw charts. It gives you the shell around them —
`shad_value_box()` and `shad_chart_container()` — and the palette inside them,
so a ggplot2, plotly, or echarts4r figure matches the page instead of fighting
it.

## KPI cards

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)

shad_value_box(
  value           = "$48,120",
  label           = "Revenue",
  delta           = "+12.4%",
  delta_direction = "up",       # "auto", "up", "down", "neutral"
  icon            = "activity",
  caption         = "vs. last month"
)
```

`delta_direction = "auto"` reads the sign off the `delta` string: a leading `-`
or `−` renders the down/destructive chip, anything else renders up. Set it
explicitly whenever "up" isn't the good direction — churn going up is not a
win.

`sparkline` takes any tag, so a small inline plot or SVG drops straight in:

```{r}
shad_value_box("1,204", "Sessions", sparkline = plotOutput("spark", height = "40px"))
```

`size` is `"sm"`, `"md"`, or `"lg"`; `href` turns the whole card into a link.

Lay them out with CSS grid — shadshiny deliberately doesn't reimplement a grid
system:

```{r}
div(
  style = "display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(12rem,1fr));gap:1rem;",
  shad_value_box("$48,120", "Revenue", delta = "+12.4%"),
  shad_value_box("1,204", "Sessions", delta = "-3.1%"),
  shad_value_box("2.4%", "Conversion", delta = "0.0%", delta_direction = "neutral")
)
```

## The chart card

```{r}
shad_chart_container(
  plotOutput("trend", height = "260px"),
  title       = "Revenue by region",
  description = "Last 6 months",
  legend      = TRUE,
  aspect      = "video"   # "video", "square", "wide", or "auto"
)
```

`aspect` locks the card's ratio. Use `"auto"` when you set an explicit height
on the plot yourself — otherwise the two fight and you get letterboxing.
`plain = TRUE` drops the card chrome and keeps only the sizing wrapper, which
is what you want when the container already sits inside a `shad_card()`.

`legend_labels` renders a legend strip in the chart palette, in order, so you
can label a plot whose own legend you suppressed:

```{r}
shad_chart_container(
  plotOutput("stack"),
  title = "Channel mix",
  legend_labels = c("Online", "Retail", "Partner")
)
```

## The palette

`shad_chart_colors(n, preset, dark)` returns `n` hex colours from the active
theme's `--shad-chart-1` … `--shad-chart-6` ramp, interpolating past six:

```{r}
shad_chart_colors(3)                        # default preset, light
shad_chart_colors(8, "blue", dark = TRUE)   # 8 colours, blue preset, dark mode
```

`shad_tokens(preset, dark)` gives you the whole token set as OKLCH strings if
you need something the chart ramp doesn't cover (`background`, `border`,
`muted-foreground`, …).

## Following the live theme

This is the part that matters. `page_shad()` themes are switched at *runtime* —
by `update_shad_theme()` or the user's dark-mode toggle — and a plot rendered
in R has no idea. `shad_current_theme()` is the bridge: a reactive read of the
browser's current theme that returns `list(preset = , dark = )`. Touch it
inside `renderPlot()` and the plot re-renders whenever the theme changes.

```{r}
output$trend <- renderPlot({
  th <- shad_current_theme()          # reactive dependency on the live theme
  ggplot2::ggplot(sales, ggplot2::aes(month, amount, colour = region)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    shad_scale_color_shad(th$preset, th$dark) +
    shad_theme_ggplot2(th$preset, th$dark)
})
```

Forget `shad_current_theme()` and your chart keeps its old colours until some
unrelated reactive happens to invalidate it.

## ggplot2

| Helper | Does |
|---|---|
| `shad_theme_ggplot2(preset, dark, base_size)` | A `theme()` matching the page: background, grid, text, and border colours. |
| `shad_scale_color_shad(preset, dark, ...)` | Discrete colour scale from the chart ramp. |
| `shad_scale_fill_shad(preset, dark, ...)` | The same, for `fill`. |

Extra `...` pass through to `ggplot2::discrete_scale()`, so `name`, `labels`,
and `guide` work as usual.

```{r}
ggplot2::ggplot(agg, ggplot2::aes(region, amount, fill = region)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  shad_scale_fill_shad(th$preset, th$dark, guide = "none") +
  shad_theme_ggplot2(th$preset, th$dark, base_size = 13) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
```

## plotly and echarts4r

These take the widget and return it, so they pipe:

```{r}
output$p <- plotly::renderPlotly({
  th <- shad_current_theme()
  plotly::plot_ly(sales, x = ~month, y = ~amount, color = ~region,
                  type = "scatter", mode = "lines") |>
    shad_theme_plotly(th$preset, th$dark)
})

output$e <- echarts4r::renderEcharts4r({
  th <- shad_current_theme()
  sales |>
    echarts4r::e_charts(month) |>
    echarts4r::e_line(amount) |>
    shad_theme_echarts4r(th$preset, th$dark)
})
```

Both `plotly` and `echarts4r` are Suggests — the helpers error with a clear
message if the package isn't installed.

## Base graphics

There is no theme helper, but the palette is just hex, so:

```{r}
output$bar <- renderPlot({
  th <- shad_current_theme()
  barplot(values, col = shad_chart_colors(length(values), th$preset, th$dark),
          border = NA)
})
```

## Timelines

For event feeds rather than figures:

```{r}
shad_timeline(
  shad_timeline_item("Order placed", time = "09:12", icon = "check",
                     description = "Payment authorised"),
  shad_timeline_item("Shipped", time = "14:40", status = "active"),
  shad_timeline_item("Delivered", time = "—", status = "muted", last = TRUE),
  align = "left"   # or "alternate"
)
```
